# Localization and copy (i18n)

Answers three things: where copy lives, what gets re-rendered when the language changes, and what rules to follow when writing new copy.

## File layout

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `web/js/strings.js` | **the i18n engine**: locale registry, resolution, `t()`, `applyCopy()`, `setLocale()`. Contains no copy itself |
| `web/js/locales/zh-CN.js` | the Simplified Chinese pack (**the source language**; `FALLBACK_GROUPS` lives here too) |
| `web/js/locales/en.js` / `ja.js` | the English/Japanese packs, key sets identical to zh-CN, character for character |
| `web/index.html` | zero copy: only `data-copy*` attributes; `#lang-select` is the top-bar switcher (with a decorative `.field-icon` globe, aria-hidden) |

## Invariants (mechanically guarded by `test/test_web_contract.py`)

1. **Copy only lives in `web/js/locales/*.js`**: a CJK literal in the engine, a panel or a template fails the test.
2. **Every pack has exactly the same key set**: one key short = that piece of UI copy disappears in some language.
3. **Each key's `{placeholders}` are consistent across languages**: translating `{n}` into `{count}` silently leaves the literal in the interpolation.
4. **Values are non-empty**; there is no empty control for a language.
5. Every `data-copy*` key in `index.html` exists in **every** pack.
6. **Backend message keys cover every frozen code** (2026-09-19, see p0-spec §4.9 supplement 4):
   warnings use `msg.<code>` (covering `test_web_contract.FROZEN_WARNING_CODES`), skip reasons use
   `msg.skip.<code>`, errors use `msg.<code>`. `app.js:localizeBackendMessage()` first checks
   `hasKey`: if there is no translation, or `t(key, params)` still leaves a `{placeholder}` (the params are incomplete),
   it **falls back to the backend's original text** - a message is never dropped, and never replaced by a bare key.

## Language resolution and switching

Priority: `?lang=` > `localStorage["kdt.lang"]` > `navigator.languages` > `zh-CN` (`normalizeTag` maps
`zh-Hans-CN`/`zh_CN`/`ja-JP` and the like to a supported tag; an unsupported language returns `null`, **without silently falling back**).

Switching is an **in-place re-render**, not a page refresh - a refresh would lose unsaved caption edits, and changing the language often happens exactly then.
`setLocale()` is responsible for: persisting → writing `documentElement.lang` → `applyCopy(document)` to relabel the static nodes →
dispatching `kdt:localechange`.

**The relabel contract (required reading when adding dynamic copy)**: any copy generated with `t()` at render time is relabeled by its panel's `relabel()`.
A panel may only redraw from **state it already holds**: send no requests, write nothing to disk, and when there is no data it must neither throw nor show an empty placeholder.
When adding a block of dynamic copy, pick one of two: register it in `relabelAfterLocaleChange()`'s component list, or accept that it stays in the old language -
the latter is a defect. `app.js` will `console.warn` when a panel lacks `relabel()`, rather than staying silent.

## Panel construction order (a defect measured in a real browser on 2026-09-19)

**Rule: the locale must be resolved before any panel is constructed.** Every panel factory in `web/js/app.js` is evaluated at **module scope**
(`createPicker` / `createGallery` / `createTagEditor` / `createFilterPanel` / `createBatchPanel` /
`createAutotagPanel` / `createExportPanel` / `createScalePanel` ...), and `t()` is called during construction and writes the string
into the DOM. So `initLocale()` must appear **before the first factory call** (right now it sits just above `const picker = createPicker(...)`).
`applyCopy()` in `boot()` relabels only static nodes carrying `data-copy*`, and `relabel()` runs only **on a switch** -
neither can rescue copy already hardcoded during construction.

Evidence (real browser, Chrome DevTools MCP driving `http://127.0.0.1:3001/?lang=en`): before the fix, the visible copy in the right-side panels contained
**103 distinct CJK segments** (filter 6 / autotag 20 / cache 3 / batch 31 / export 33 / scale 30). Control experiment: switching the language
zh-CN → en fixed only filter and autotag (leaving just the Batch/Export/Scale tab labels), while the batch/export/scale panels
**were still entirely Chinese** - their tab buttons and section copy were hardcoded at construction time, and nothing relabels them on a language switch.
`initLocale()` only reads `window.location` / `localStorage` / `navigator` and writes `document.documentElement.lang`,
all of which exist while a `type=module` script is being evaluated, so putting it at module scope is safe; `boot()` no longer calls it again.

**Tab labels hardcoded at construction time must be covered by `relabel()`.** A panel's tab buttons and `fieldset` / `legend` / `label` copy
are generated with `t()` during construction: give the panel a `relabel()` that registers each piece of construction-time copy as a painter
(`paintText` / `paintAttr`, with the `t()` call written only inside the painter, the key no longer repeated at the switch site), and in
`relabelAfterLocaleChange()` call `relabelComponent(...)` **unconditionally** - not only `onShow()` when its own tab happens to be active,
because on a language switch that tab usually isn't. `relabel()` still redraws only from held state, sends no requests,
and doesn't throw when there is no data.

Criteria: `test/test_web_i18n.py::test_locale_is_resolved_before_any_panel_is_constructed` (pins that `initLocale()`
appears before the first `create...(`, exactly once), `test_every_dynamic_panel_is_relabelled_on_a_switch`
(batchPanel/exportPanel/scalePanel must be registered unconditionally **before** the tab branch),
`test_panels_built_at_module_scope_expose_relabel`, and the behavior fixture `test/fixtures/panel_locale_harness.mjs`
(locale resolves to en and construction happens after; tab labels / legend / placeholder must be English; after switching to zh-CN, `relabel()` must
relabel them back to Chinese, with zero requests throughout). All four were falsified: moving `initLocale()` / making the locale resolve late / tearing out the `paintLabels()`
inside `relabel()` / moving the registration into the tab branch → each turns red respectively, and all are green after restoring.

## Adding a language

1. Copy `locales/zh-CN.js` to `locales/<tag>.js` and change only the values, **not the keys and placeholders**;
2. Add a row to `LOCALES` in `strings.js` (`label` uses **the language's own name**, never translated - someone who can't read the current UI
   must still recognize their own language);
3. Run `pytest test/test_web_contract.py test/test_web_i18n.py -q`.

## UX writing rules

**The wording rules live in [ui-copy](ui-copy.md)** - terminology, punctuation and spacing per language, the length budget,
and the button / error / empty-state / status templates. Read it before changing any string in a pack.

What stays in this topic is the mechanism: copy lives only in the packs (invariant 1 above), render-time copy must be
registered for relabel, and the two writing-related checks are `test_one_word_per_concept` (the concept table is in
[ui-copy](ui-copy.md)) and `test_glyph_only_labels_carry_an_accessible_name` (a single-glyph label needs a
`data-copy-aria`) - both listed under Criteria below, with their falsification.

## Criteria

- `test/test_web_contract.py` - invariants 1/2/3/4 + key drift (`t("...")`, `data-copy*`, dynamic prefixes).
- `test/test_web_i18n.py` + `test/fixtures/i18n_harness.mjs` - wiring, `data-copy` existence across packs,
  and really running the engine (fake DOM + fake localStorage): resolution priority, `setLocale` persistence/notification/relabel, `applyCopy`.
- `test/test_web_*.py` (12 of them) - when asserting Chinese copy they read `locales/zh-CN.js`, no longer `strings.js`.
- Accessibility and terminology: `test/test_web_i18n.py`'s `test_glyph_only_labels_carry_an_accessible_name`
  and `test_one_word_per_concept`. Both were falsified (removing `data-copy-aria` / stuffing in a synonym → red).

## Deliberate boundaries

- **Modal layers are not in the relabel list**: `picker.js` (the directory chooser dialog) and `zoom.js` (the zoom preview) render their copy when opened,
  and don't relabel on a language switch. They cover the top bar while open, so the user can't reach `#lang-select` at all - that window is unreachable.
  If they are later made non-modal (or a keyboard-reachable switch entry point is added), `relabel()` must be added.
- **Streaming status lines are not relabeled**: autotag/scale progress lines come from SSE and the panel doesn't retain them; relabeling a cached tick would
  roll a finished job back to "in progress". Those strings are fetched with `t()` when the event arrives, so they are already in the new language.

## Backend message localization (an incremental structure)

The backend no longer needs to know the UI language: it keeps producing its original strings and **additionally** provides a structured form.

| Location | Incremental field | Frontend rendering |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /api/dataset/toml` | `warning_items: [{code, params, text}]`, `skipped_items: [{image_dir, code, params, reason}]` | `t("msg." + code, params)`, `msg.skip.*` for skipped |
| any error response | `error.params` | `t("msg." + code, params)` |

The old fields `warnings` / `skipped[].reason` / `error.message` are **unchanged, character for character**; their role is a **degradation fallback**:
the structured fields are the source of truth, and the fallback strings are a pure projection of them (produced in one place in core, compared byte-for-byte by tests).
**The fallbacks cannot be deleted** - diagnostic messages (`validation_error` / `internal_error` / the various 500s) are intentionally untranslated under this section's rule,
and deleting the fallbacks would make them render as blanks. Field responsibilities and invariants are in [p0-spec](p0-spec.md) §4.
Frontend rendering always goes through `localizeBackendMessage(prefix, code, params)`, which returns `null` and falls back to the backend's original text in **two** cases:
(a) there is no translation for that code; (b) the translation still contains an unfilled `{placeholder}` (meaning the params are incomplete, in which case the backend's original text is more complete).
So a message is **never lost and never displayed as a bare key**.

**The structured fill-in on 2026-09-19 (structured data is the source of truth)**: `PathOutsideRoots` in `core/paths.py`
now carries `code` / `params` itself - unconfigured allowlist `paths_unconfigured` (empty params),
path resolution failure `bad_path`, out-of-bounds `outside_roots` (`{"path": str}`). Every api site and
`app.py`'s exception handlers pass these two fields **through unchanged**, no longer hardcoding code/message themselves;
the `not_found` / `not_a_directory` sites each carry `{"path": ...}` too. So
`outside_roots` / `not_found` / `not_a_directory` **are no longer localizable only through the `dataset.toml` route**:
every endpoint that produces them now carries the placeholders `msg.<code>` needs, and the old `message` is still a permanent fallback.

## Model description localization (2026-09-19)

WD14 model-list descriptions are the same kind of thing as backend messages: `registry.BUILTIN[].description` is hardcoded original prose,
**kept permanently** as a degradation fallback; the source of truth is a localized key looked up **by stable id**,
`autotag.model.desc.<model-id>`.

**The model id is a stable key.** `description` is prose and drifts as wording is rewritten - using it as a key means changing one word
silently drops the whole translation.

Both frontend sites follow the same rule (`autotag.js`):

    const key = "autotag.model.desc." + model.id;
    const text = hasKey(key) ? t(key) : String(model.description || "");

- `paintModelList()` - the model list rows;
- `paintModelNote()` - the note below the dropdown (re-derived from the held models; `relabel()` already registers
  `paintModelList()` and `paintModelNote()`, so a language switch refreshes them).

When a translation is missing it shows `description` **verbatim**: the message is never hidden and never replaced by a bare key. When adding a built-in model,
add an `autotag.model.desc.<new id>` entry to each of the three packs. The sizes in the original `description` ("445.8 MB", "about 1.2 GB")
are **no longer repeated** - size is `size_bytes` / `download_size_bytes` data, not copy.

Criteria: `test/test_web_i18n.py::test_every_builtin_model_description_is_localised_in_every_pack`
(model ids are derived from `registry.BUILTIN`, not copied a second time in the test; a pack passes only when every one is non-empty).

**The blind spot this exposed (important)**: the contract test guards "no CJK outside `web/js/locales/`" - which covers only
text **the frontend itself produces**. Prose **the backend produces and the frontend passes through** is simply outside its jurisdiction: the model descriptions
slipped through exactly that way; and even if that prose were all English it wouldn't catch it either (the criterion only recognizes CJK). So for every field added that
"returns prose from the backend for the frontend to display", you must give it its own **id-keyed** key, plus a criterion that "every id has a key in **every** pack".

**A dead field fixed along the way**: `download_size_bytes` (§4.7's static nominal download size) previously **had no frontend code reading it**
- an uninstalled row read only the local `size_bytes` (always 0), so it displayed "unknown size". Removing the sizes duplicated in the descriptions
is what exposed this; now both the list rows and the download-progress start use it, with the criterion pinned in
`test_web_contract.py::test_model_list_shows_installed_downloadable_and_blocked`, and it **pins the use site
rather than the literal's existence** (the first version of the criterion tested existence only, so changing the use site stayed green - the pit this repository keeps stepping in).

## Known gaps (next steps)

1. **17 error codes are intentionally untranslated**, falling back to the backend's original text in an English/Japanese UI (the fallback exists for exactly these):
   `bad_request, cache_dir_inside_roots, cannot_plan, conflict, decode_failed, forbidden,
   internal_error, invalid_tag, method_not_allowed, model_load_failed, model_unavailable, scan_failed,
   unauthorized, unavailable, unknown_model, validation_error, write_failed`.
   Three kinds of reason: (a) diagnostics and raw exception text - `validation_error` / `internal_error` are pydantic / exception errors,
   and the messages of `write_failed` / `scan_failed` / `cache_dir_inside_roots` / `decode_failed` /
   `model_load_failed` embed `str(exc)`, so translating them would lose debugging information; (b) the generic HTTP statuses
   `forbidden` / `unauthorized` / `method_not_allowed` / `conflict` / `unavailable`
   have no specific content to translate; (c) `bad_request` / `invalid_tag` / `unknown_model` /
   `model_unavailable` / `cannot_plan` are free text like `str(exc)`. The three **API call** sites where `bad_request`
   carries a fixed template have been split into their own codes (see below); but the two that the config layer raises via
   `PathConfigError` and the §4.11 `/api/roots` endpoint surfaces (`path must not be empty`, `cannot resolve path %r: %s`)
   **still use the original-text fallback** -
   their code is still the frozen `bad_request` (**not renamed**, since renaming would turn `test_roots_api` red),
   so they still display the backend's original wording; `params` now passes through the exception object (`cannot resolve path` carries `{"path", "detail"}`),
   which is the structured half, not a translation.
   There is exactly one criterion: translate only when **the message is a fixed template and the variables are provided as `params`**; free text and diagnostics always keep their original wording.

   2026-09-19 localized all the **actionable fixed-template 4xx** messages: `not_a_file`, `unsupported_image`,
   `bad_size`, `bad_write_mode`, `bad_op`, `unknown_job`, `no_images`, `unreadable`,
   plus `missing_tag_payload` / `empty_image_list` / `bad_path` split out of `bad_request`;
   per-code `params` are in [p0-spec](p0-spec.md) §4.9 supplement 4. The old `message` / fallback strings are unchanged, character for character.
   Adding a new localizable error takes two steps: add `params=` to `error_response(...)`, then add `msg.<code>` to the three language packs.
2. **`api/autotag.py`'s `errors[].message` is not translated**: that is the raw text thrown by the inference/download libraries (often an English exception),
   kept as diagnostic information; the labels in the UI are already localized.
3. **Batch editing's per-image `results[].error` is not translated**: each error in `captions.py`'s batch results is still the backend's original text,
   and the frontend's `batch.js` renders `entry.error.message` directly - it doesn't take the `error_response` shape and has no code/params channel.
   Localizing it would need a code+params scheme first (like `_check_image`'s); that is out of scope for now.
4. **Real-browser switching has already been run (2026-09-19)**: Chrome DevTools MCP drove `?lang=en` and switched zh-CN ↔ en;
   the construction-order defect and the batch/export/scale non-relabel problem were exactly what that run discovered - see "Panel construction order" above.
